newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-Lomu means business, Hart tells poms.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Lomu means business, Hart tells poms.

text.p: LONDON, Nov 21 - You wouldn't need to be a rocket scientist to figure out that one name was on the lips of British journalists turning up to cover the arrival of the New Zealand Barbarians rugby team in London yesterday -- Jonah Lomu.
And coach John Hart, bailed up by six English journalists for the latest developments in the life of the giant winger after a brief press conference, wasn't in a mood to disappoint anyone.
Yes Lomu is fine, yes his year has been disappointing, of course he hoped that he isn't a spent force in world rugby.
And Hart, perhaps with one mischievous eye on the All Black tour of Britain next year, wasn't about to let the chance slip to give the British something to write about on Lomu.

Not that he needs to. One English newspaper is prompting bets from other journalists that it will average one Lomu story per day on the 11-day tour. So far it is one ahead, having run one before the team even arrived.

English rugby, and its rugby press, has been in awe of the 21-year-old since he swatted aside Tony Underwood, shrugged off Will Carling and trampled over Mike Catt to score the opening try of the teams' World Cup semifinal last year.
No matter that he'd done much the same against Ireland, Wales and Scotland before that. When he did it against England, THAT was news for the English press.
This year, the journalists pointed out, Lomu hasn't featured much at international level, so is he a spent force?
"Oh no, I shouldn't think so," Hart laughed. "At the age of 22 I would hope not."
And he added: "I think 1997 will be a big year for him."
Even bigger than 1995? ventured one reporter.
"Oh yes," Hart continued. "1995 I think was only about five or six matches when you think about it. I believe he needs a full season to really show what he can do.
"You may see a different dimension in his game in future," he added tantalisingly, without elaborating.
On a more serious note, Hart said that Lomu has had a demanding year with off-field distractions, getting married (twice) and also experiencing injury.
"It has been a difficult year for him, but a character-building year," he said.
"I think he will come back and be a better person, and a better player, for it.
"I think that when he came on the scene last year we had never seen anything like him in New Zealand rugby, or in world rugby for that matter.
"It has taken him time to adjust to the attention, to being in the public eye all the time.
"There have been a couple of off-field incidents, then he got injured. But he is back now and I expect to see him at his best here."
English rugby doesn't have to wait long now for its first taste of Lomu.
With Hart keen to give as many of his first-choice players as possible a run against Northern Counties on Sunday, he is likely to be in the starting 15.
